This is a ghost light, and it was originally created for a theater in southern Vermont during the pandemic.
It was sort of the porch light for the theater while it was dark, to show that it's still alive even though it's not open.
It uses images from the theater's archive of 50 years of performances.
The materials around it are basically optical materials that just keep changing with light.
It's powered by wind. There's a little fan in the corner that provides air currents that change.
And depending on where you stand, it changes your...
the motion.
It's a very low-tech approach.
All the colors are generated with optically reactive materials like diffraction grating,
Fresnel lenses, fabric that creates moire patterns.
So they're all active color. They're not passive, reflective color.
So it's really quite a dynamic, you know, sculpture.
When I contacted the theater, I told them about the project, and I said,
What I need are 20 images that are iconic theater pictures, kind of universal poses or combinations of actors that I could incorporate into the piece.
And the art director at the theater went through their history and found 20 images from 50 years of performances.
It was a very nice gift from the theater.
And also, I gave them a very nice gift for three months.
